cobw_001.sourceTitle: Why Smart People Keep Going Broke
cobw_001.sourcePremise: High income does not necessarily create financial resilience. Smart people often optimize the wrong variables and mistake complexity for control.

cobw_002.sourceTitle: Why Getting a Raise Doesn't Make You Rich
cobw_002.sourcePremise: Lifestyle creep and fixed obligations absorb marginal income faster than most people expect, so higher pay rarely changes the balance sheet.

cobw_003.sourceTitle: How a Six-Figure Salary Can Still Leave You Broke
cobw_003.sourcePremise: Fixed costs, debt service, and social spending scale with income in ways that keep cash flow tight even at high nominal wages.

cobw_004.sourceTitle: Why Looking Wealthy Can Make You Poor
cobw_004.sourcePremise: Status spending and visible consumption trade long-term net worth for short-term signals, often without a deliberate choice.

cobw_005.sourceTitle: The Hidden Tax of Financial Overthinking
cobw_005.sourcePremise: Analysis paralysis and constant optimization burn attention and delay decisions that matter more than perfect information.

cobw_006.sourceTitle: Why Emergency Funds Feel Impossible Until They Don't
cobw_006.sourcePremise: Buffer savings fail when treated as a moral achievement instead of a cash-flow design problem.

cobw_007.sourceTitle: When "Good Debt" Becomes a Story You Tell Yourself
cobw_007.sourcePremise: Leverage labels hide risk concentration and reduce the urgency to build flexibility.

cobw_008.sourceTitle: Why Budget Apps Fail Knowledge Workers
cobw_008.sourcePremise: Irregular income and cognitive load break category-based budgeting unless the system matches how decisions are actually made.

cobw_009.sourceTitle: The Real Cost of Comparison Spending
cobw_009.sourcePremise: Reference groups shift silently when income rises, keeping satisfaction flat while spending climbs.

cobw_010.sourcePremise: Generic rules ignore constraints, values conflict, and the emotional weight of money decisions.

cobw_011.sourceTitle: Focus Debt Is Real (And You Are Paying Interest)
cobw_011.sourcePremise: Unfinished cognitive threads and context switching compound like interest on attention.

cobw_012.sourceTitle: Why Multitasking Feels Productive and Isn't
cobw_012.sourcePremise: Rapid task switching creates activity without progress on work that requires depth.

cobw_013.sourcePremise: Interrupt-driven workflows train brains to expect novelty, making sustained concentration feel unnatural.

cobw_014.sourceTitle: Why Your Calendar Is Stealing Your Focus
cobw_014.sourcePremise: Fragmented schedules leave no contiguous blocks for hard problems, so shallow work expands to fill the gaps.

cobw_015.sourceTitle: Deep Work Requires Environmental Design, Not Willpower
cobw_015.sourcePremise: Relying on discipline alone fails when the default environment rewards distraction.

cobw_016.sourceTitle: Why Open Offices Destroy More Than Productivity
cobw_016.sourcePremise: Constant visibility changes what people work on, not just how fast they finish tasks.

cobw_017.sourceTitle: The Cost of Always Being Available
cobw_017.sourcePremise: Responsiveness signals reliability but erodes boundaries that protect quality and recovery.

cobw_018.sourceTitle: Why Burnout Looks Like Laziness From the Outside
cobw_018.sourcePremise: Depletion reduces initiative before it reduces hours, so output drops while effort feels unchanged.

cobw_019.sourceTitle: Meeting Culture Is a Hidden Payroll Tax
cobw_019.sourcePremise: Synchronous coordination scales poorly; organizations pay twice in salaries and lost focus.

cobw_020.sourceTitle: Why Promotions Can Make Work Harder
cobw_020.sourcePremise: New scope adds coordination and emotional labor that raw skill does not prepare you for.

cobw_021.sourceTitle: Remote Work Didn't Fail—Your Defaults Did
cobw_021.sourcePremise: Without intentional structure, home and office both amplify the same attention leaks.

cobw_022.sourceTitle: The Myth of the 40-Hour Knowledge Job
cobw_022.sourcePremise: Creative and analytical work does not compress linearly; extra hours often buy rework, not results.

cobw_023.sourcePremise: "I am the kind of person who…" collapses when life context shifts, leaving no fallback behavior.

cobw_024.sourcePremise: All-or-nothing rules create predictable rebound behavior that feels like personal failure.

cobw_025.sourceTitle: Why Habit Trackers Stop Working After Week Three
cobw_025.sourcePremise: Measurement without friction redesign becomes admin work, not behavior change.

cobw_026.sourcePremise: Cue redesign is cheaper than repeated self-negotiation, but people keep buying inspiration instead.

cobw_027.sourceTitle: The Cost of "Just One More Episode"
cobw_027.sourcePremise: Variable rewards and easy continuation exploit the same delay-discounting that breaks savings goals.

cobw_028.sourceTitle: Why Morning Routines Break on Travel Days
cobw_028.sourcePremise: Rigid sequences fail without portable minimum viable habits.

cobw_029.sourceTitle: Decision Fatigue at the Grocery Store
cobw_029.sourcePremise: Micro-decisions deplete the same pool you need for harder choices later in the day.

cobw_030.sourcePremise: Optimizing the system substitutes for doing the uncomfortable task the system was meant to support.
